description: Reconcile internally booked payments against payment-processor settlements by payment reference. The processor can settle one payment in several partial settlement rows, and the internal ledger can hold several rows per reference (corrections); aggregate each side per reference first. Then classify every reference found on either side: 'matched' when both sides exist and ABS(internal - processor) <= 0.01; 'amount_mismatch' when both exist and the difference is larger; 'missing_in_processor' when only the internal side exists; 'missing_in_internal' when only the processor side exists. Rows with a NULL reference on either side are excluded from matching. Output columns: reference (STRING), internal_amount (FLOAT64), processor_amount (FLOAT64), difference (FLOAT64, internal minus processor, 2 decimals; NULL when one side is missing), status (STRING). Sort by reference.

reference.description: Payment reference shared with the processor

amount.description: Booked amount; corrections are separate signed rows

reference.description: Payment reference; NULL for processor fees

amount.description: Settled amount; a payment may be split across rows

edge_cases: r1 is settled in two parts (60 + 40) and must match the single internal booking of 100
Floating point sums need the 0.01 tolerance rather than strict equality
References present on only one side must be reported from both directions
Processor fee rows with NULL reference must not appear or be matched to each other
common_failure_modes: FM1: FULL OUTER JOIN on raw rows duplicates the internal 100 against both settlement rows and reports two mismatches
FM1: LEFT JOIN from the internal side never reveals r4 (missing_in_internal)
FM5: COALESCE(amount, 0) before classification turns a missing side into an amount_mismatch instead of a missing_* status
